              MOTION TO RESCIND SHOW CAUSE ORDER
    ON BEHALF OF THE CITIES OF ANAHEIM, AZUSA, BANNING, COLTON,
               PASADENA, AND RIVERSIDE, CALIFORNIA


           Pursuant to Rule 212 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 1 the Cities of

Anaheim, Azusa, Banning, Colton, Pasadena, and Riverside, California (collectively, the “Six



1
    18 C.F.R. § 385.212 (2026).



                                                 -1-
 Cities”) hereby submit this motion to rescind the show cause order issued by the Commission in

the above-referenced proceeding on June 18, 2026,2 as directed to each of the Six Cities as

Participating Transmission Owners (“TOs”) in the California Independent System Operator

Corporation (“CAISO”).

         I.      DESCRIPTION OF THE SIX CITIES

              Each of the Six Cities operates a municipal electric system that is located within the

CAISO Balancing Authority Area. The Cities are each electrically surrounded by Southern

California Edison Company (“SCE”), which is an Original Participating TO 3 in the CAISO.

Although each of the Cities has made arrangements to obtain energy and capacity from a variety

of resources, the Cities are dependent upon the CAISO and SCE for the delivery of the majority

of these resources.

              The Cities of Anaheim, Azusa, Banning, and Riverside became Participating TOs in the

CAISO and signed the Transmission Control Agreement (“TCA”) among and between the

CAISO and its Participating TOs effective January 1, 2003. The City of Pasadena executed the

TCA and became a Participating TO as of January 1, 2005, and the City of Colton executed the

TCA and became a Participating TO as of January 1, 2013. As Participating TOs in the CAISO,

each of the Cities has transferred to the CAISO’s Operational Control certain transmission

facilities and Entitlements, and they each have a TO Tariff on file with the Commission that

establishes rates, terms, and conditions of service on their facilities and Entitlements consistent

with the CAISO Tariff and the TCA. In general, the Six Cities’ facilities and Entitlements over

which the CAISO has assumed Operational Control represent either shares of jointly-owned

 facilities with, in some cases, entities that are not CAISO Participating TOs and/or are likewise

not Commission-jurisdictional, or contractual rights to transmission service on other parties’

systems, which are governed by the terms and conditions of those parties’ tariffs and/or bilateral

transmission service agreements.

        II.      RELEVANT BACKGROUND

              On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued the Show Cause Order, thereby initiating a

proceeding under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act. The Show Cause Order found that the

CAISO Tariff and/or the TO Tariffs of each of the CAISO Participating TOs appear to be unjust,

unreasonable, or unduly discriminatory or preferential to the extent that they do not include

provisions establishing the rates, terms, and conditions for the interconnection of and service to

certain large and co-located loads. The Show Cause Order therefore directed the CAISO and the

CAISO Participating TOs to either explain how their respective tariffs remain just and

reasonable without specific provisions for the interconnection of large and co-located loads or to

develop such provisions. 4

       III.      JUSTIFICATION FOR RESCISSION

              Each of the Six Cities is a non-public utility that is exempt from the Commission’s

jurisdiction pursuant to Section 201(f) of the Federal Power Act. 5 The Commission

acknowledged that the Show Cause Order included Participating TOs that are not subject to the

Commission’s jurisdiction and explained that it would “rescind the show cause order” against

such entities at their request, provided that the CAISO “respond[s] to this order regarding the




4
    Show Cause Order at P 3.
5
 16 U.S.C. 824(f) (2024), City of Anaheim, 171 FERC ¶ 61,263, at PP 19-22 (2020), cited in Show Cause Order at P
3, n.9.



                                                     -3-
 non-public utility’s CAISO Tariff provisions on file with the Commission.”6 Accordingly, as

non-public utilities, the Six Cities request that the Commission rescind the Show Cause Order

against each of the Six Cities.

              In requesting recission of the Show Cause Order, the Six Cities will coordinate and

cooperate with the CAISO in responding to the Show Cause Order, to the extent that the CAISO

requests assistance from the Six Cities and with respect to provisions in the Cities’ TO Tariffs

that pertain to load interconnections.7 The Six Cities have conferred with the CAISO and are

authorized to state that the CAISO supports this motion. The Six Cities also acknowledge the

Commission’s authority to review their transmission revenue requirements as set forth in their

TO Tariffs to ensure the CAISO’s rates remain just and reasonable. 8 Consistent with the Cities’

practice, if any of the Cities determines that changes to its TO Tariff are needed to address the

issues in the Show Cause Order or any other topics, each City will file proposed revisions to its

TO Tariff with the Commission.9

     IV.      CONCLUSION

          WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, the Six Cities respectfully request that the

Commission rescind the Show Cause Order against each of the Cities as non-public utilities and

ask that the Commission waive any notice and comment periods that might be applicable to this

motion.
